synthetic.name: Polysilicon Production
synthetic.notes: Xinjiang province alone accounts for approximately 40% of global polysilicon manufacturing capacity. UFLPA (US Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act) and related import restrictions have specifically targeted Xinjiang-sourced polysilicon since 2021-2022 due to documented forced-labor concerns, creating a structural compliance-cost and opacity gap. D-heavy: constraint load (feedstock purity specs, energy intensity, labour-sourcing scrutiny) exceeds contribution capacity.
synthetic.data_quality: Low-Medium: aggregate capacity is public (IEA), but facility-level labor and sourcing data is largely opaque

synthetic.name: Ingot and Wafer Manufacturing
synthetic.notes: BOTTLENECK, worst phase in chain. China holds approximately 95-98% of global ingot and wafer capacity, up from about 80% in 2010. Extreme single-point concentration: one out of every seven solar panels produced worldwide is manufactured by a single facility. Low transparency at the facility ownership and supply-contract level.
synthetic.data_quality: Low: facility-level ownership and supply-contract data not publicly disclosed; aggregate capacity shares from IEA and industry trackers

synthetic.name: Cell Manufacturing
synthetic.notes: China's cell manufacturing share rose from about 60% in 2010 to almost 80-85% by the early 2020s. In 2010 the cell market was more diversified: Chinese Taipei 14%, Japan 7%, Germany 6%. Medium-high transparency: production volumes tracked by industry associations (e.g. BloombergNEF, PV InfoLink).
synthetic.data_quality: Medium-High: production volumes tracked by industry associations

synthetic.name: Module Assembly
synthetic.notes: Most geographically diverse stage in the chain. Southeast Asian countries (Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam) plus a growing US and India assembly base provide partial diversification, even though China remains dominant at roughly 80%. High transparency: trade and customs data are public.
synthetic.data_quality: High: trade and customs data are public

synthetic.name: Installation and Grid Connection
synthetic.notes: Utility-scale and distributed rooftop installation, interconnection to grid. Medium-high transparency: installed capacity tracked nationally by IEA and national energy agencies.

synthetic.name: End-of-Life and Recycling
synthetic.notes: Secondary bottleneck. Under 10% of retired panels are formally recycled through mandated take-back or recycling infrastructure in most markets (PROVISIONAL estimate); most jurisdictions lack mandated take-back schemes. Low transparency: end-of-life volumes and disposal pathways are poorly tracked globally.
synthetic.data_quality: Low: end-of-life volumes and disposal pathways poorly tracked globally; recycling rate figure is a PROVISIONAL estimate

metrics.mandated_take_back_schemes: Rare; not present in most jurisdictions

system.interpretation: The solar PV supply chain scores 79.0% chain average balance, just below the 80% Good/Coherent threshold. Phase 1 (Ingot and Wafer Manufacturing, 65.0%) is the worst-performing phase and the most geographically concentrated stage in the entire chain: China holds approximately 95-98% of global capacity, and one in seven solar panels worldwide comes from a single facility. Phase 0 (Polysilicon Production, 67.7%) is the second-worst phase, driven by Xinjiang's approximately 40% share of global polysilicon capacity and the structural compliance and opacity gap created by UFLPA forced-labor import restrictions since 2021-2022. Phase 5 (End-of-Life and Recycling, 73.1%) is a secondary stressed phase: under 10% of retired panels are formally recycled in most markets. The defining structural feature of this chain is that China's manufacturing share exceeds 80% at every stage, more than double its 36% share of global PV demand: a proportional value-distribution failure documented in the phi-axis score.

baseline.label: Current state (2026 baseline, PROVISIONAL)
baseline.notes: pi = chain average balance across 6 phases (79.0, just below Good/Coherent threshold). phi = proportional value distribution: China captures over 80% of manufacturing value across every stage while holding only 36% of global demand, the sharpest phi-failure of any chain in this repository's corpus (Stressed zone, close to the 61.8% Failure boundary). sqrt2 = structural overhead: single-facility concentration (1 in 7 panels), and UFLPA compliance costs are documented structural friction (Stressed zone). ln2 = growth and transformation: solar PV has the strongest cost-decline and technology-conversion track record of any energy technology in the corpus (Coherent zone). e = financial abstraction: national tariffs, IRA 45X and EU Net Zero Industry Act tax credits, and anti-dumping duties exist but are inconsistently linked to physical supply-chain diversification outcomes (Stressed zone). The phi-axis score (60.0) is the standout failure signal for this chain and is the headline diagnostic finding.
